dedupe_keys.name: osemosys open source energy modelling system

description: OSeMOSYS, the Open Source Energy Modelling System, is a long-term energy system optimisation framework. Its website lists uses in power sector capacity expansion, transport sector planning, regional energy integration across several countries, sector coupling such as Power-to-X, climate, land, energy and water (CLEW) analysis and economic policy analysis of investment, costs and emissions. The reference implementation in GNU MathProg is run with the GLPK solver (glpsol) or the GUSEK environment, for example on the UTOPIA training case, and the repository runs regression and harmonisation tests across its normal and short implementations with pytest. The citation file lists Mark Howells, Manuel Welsch (with an International Atomic Energy Agency affiliation) and others as authors. The code is free under the Apache 2.0 licence on GitHub; the MathProg repository had tags up to v1.0.1 and its last commit on 16 April 2024, while the wider community maintains other implementations and learning material. Coverage is any country or region the user parameterises. Caveats: model results depend entirely on user data, and the MathProg version needs a linear programming solver. Simulation uses are least-cost capacity expansion and supply security scenarios for national power and energy systems. Related records: model-temoa and model-calliope are other open energy system optimisation models.
